De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=4$ and $\phi =5\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )]^{4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 5\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
